text.p: Italian bond markets started mixed with cash bonds making small gains while futures slipped back in line with other European bond markets.
Dealers said that there were signs of some consolidation after Wednesday's sharp BTP rise after German July jobless data which the market interpreted as seeing a German rate rise as less likely.
"The mood is cautious this morning, but with T-bonds holding to better level overnight, there is no reason BTP futures can not push ahead today," said one LIFFE dealer.

In the U.S., T-bonds closed higher overnight and now awaits the last 30-year bond leg of its three-day Treasury auction later today, while in Italy Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi urged greater progress towards Europe's single currency, stressing that Italy was ready to join at the 1999 start date.
In early trade, the Sept LIFFE BTP futures pushed into positive territory, and was 15 basis points up at 135.87 at 0750 GMT.
